The only production callers of `LocationService.saveLocation` in the REST module are two resource classes, `LocationResource1_8.save` and `LocationAttributeResource1_9`'s `save` and `delete`. Three tests in `LocationController1_9Test` also call it directly. The repo is `openmrs-module-webservices.rest` in Falkon (the name without the `github.com/openmrs/` prefix didn't resolve on the first try).

1. **`LocationResource1_8.save(Location)`** (lines 218–224) returns `Context.getLocationService().saveLocation(location)`. This is the main path: it is the `DelegatingCrudResource` save hook for `/location` create and update, so any change to how `saveLocation` persists, validates or returns a location hits every location write through the REST API.
2. **`LocationAttributeResource1_9.save(LocationAttribute)`** (lines 85–103) adds the attribute to its parent location, then calls `saveLocation(delegate.getLocation())` to persist it.
3. **`LocationAttributeResource1_9.delete(...)`** (lines 109–114) soft-deletes an attribute by setting it voided and then calls `saveLocation(delegate.getLocation())`. A change to voiding or saving semantics affects this.
4. **`LocationController1_9Test.shouldIncludeTheListOfChildLocations`** (lines 236–250) saves a location with a new child, then checks the representation.
5. **`LocationController1_9Test.shouldIncludeTheParentLocation`** (lines 220–234) sets a parent and calls `saveLocation` before a GET.
6. **`LocationController1_9Test.shouldOverwriteAListOfChildLocations`** (lines 159–174) adds a child, saves, then POSTs an empty `childLocations` list and checks the result.

The test callers would only be affected if the behaviour change alters the persisted state these tests set up, so they are less likely to break than the production callers.
